The bug: Go slices are passed by value, so the recursive `search` extends a local copy of the slice header and `MakeChain` returns its stale length-1 header. I'll make `search` return the chain explicitly.

Wait, there's still a subtle issue: `try` truncates `chain` after search returns — but the returned `c` is a slice header pointing to the same backing array with the full length. Truncating the local `chain` header doesn't affect `c`'s header. Good.

But there's another subtle issue: when search returns `chain` (the full header), and then the caller's `try` truncates its own header — no problem, `c` retains the full length. And `MakeChain` returns `c`. Good.

All tests pass. The implementation in `dominoes.go`:

- **`Domino`** is defined as `[2]int` (a pair of halves).
- **`MakeChain`** tries each domino as the chain's starting point, then **`search`** does a backtracking DFS: at each step it extends the open end with any unused domino whose matching half fits, in both orientations. When all dominoes are placed, it accepts the chain only if the last free half matches the first (`chain[0][0] == chain[len-1][1]`).
- The search returns the completed chain slice explicitly, since Go passes slice headers by value — the first version returned a stale length-1 header from `MakeChain` and failed the "wrong length chain" check.

This handles the tricky cases in `cases_test.go`: backtracking past dead ends ("need backtrack"), rejecting disconnected sets that still have all-even vertex degrees ("disconnected - *" cases), and allowing duplicate stones since each input element is tracked by index. `go test` and `go vet` are both clean.
